text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.8% today after falling 6.97% over two weeks, rebounding on tentative signs of de-escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions. Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran aimed at restarting U.S.-Iran negotiations, which could ease concerns about potential disruptions to global oil supplies — a worry that had pushed the stock down sharply earlier in the week when tensions appeared to be rising.

The rebound also reflects the company's underlying strength: U.S. oil refining capacity is running at 92.8% utilization with tight fuel inventories (gasoline storage at 209 million barrels), which typically boosts refiner margins. That said, the company just announced a leadership change on October 29th, and investors are watching closely to see what new guidance management will provide amid the tension between record refining profits and political pressure on Big Oil to justify high fuel prices.
